stemMd: A reserve manager says a new fence increased bird nesting success because more nests survived after installation. Which information is most important to evaluating that argument?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Whether the fence was the most expensive available.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Whether weather conditions affecting nesting were unusually favorable after the fence was installed.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Whether the fence is visible from the road.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Whether the reserve has a visitor shop.

explanationMd: A before-and-after causal claim needs investigation of competing causes. Favorable weather could increase nest survival without the fence. Learning whether that competing explanation applies changes the strength of the attribution.

distractorRationale.a: Price does not isolate its effect on nest survival.
distractorRationale.e: Personal interest is not the relevant alternative cause.
distractorRationale.d: The shop has no stated bearing on nesting.
distractorRationale.c: Visibility does not establish predation or survival effects.
